title: The Besieged Singhs Choose Assault over Dishonor

blocks.text: With provisions thinning and pressure mounting, the Khalsa refuses the idea of saving itself through flight or humiliation. The page states the choice in martial terms: better to die fighting than flee in disgrace when the Panth’s honor is already on trial before the world.

That resolve becomes action in coordinated assaults against Mughal posts. The defenders strike from one side, seize positions where they can, and try to turn a siege into a series of sudden local reversals that keep the enemy off balance.

Even when losses mount, the example draws in more fighters rather than breaking morale. Ram Rauni thus appears not merely as a fort under pressure but as a school of disciplined self-sacrifice in which one wave of Singhs replaces another.
